title: The Marriage Is Restored and Delhi Hears of the Khalsa

blocks.text: The Khalsa completes the work it had begun for the rescued woman. Because the Panth had accepted her as their own daughter, contributions are gathered for an adequate dowry and the Brahmin household leaves the camp with gratitude rather than ruin.

News of the intervention then spreads far beyond the immediate family. Hindus celebrate the fact that the Sayyad was slaughtered, while Muslims report with alarm that the Khalsa has moved to the area surrounding Delhi and is no longer content to remain at a distance.
The page turns a single act of protection into a wider political tremor. A sense of panic gripped the inhabitants of Delhi because the Panth now appears both morally resolute and militarily near.
